result.topic_en: Computations in surface theory relating the Laplacian of log m to a determinant Δ formed from the coefficients A, B, C and their derivatives, together with differentiation formulas for na and nα and resulting expressions for m'' n'', n', m', m''.
result.transcription:
$mm\left(\frac{\partial\partial \log m}{\partial t^2}+\frac{\partial\partial\log m}{\partial u^2}\right) = -(aA'+bB'+cC')(\alpha A''+\beta B''+\gamma C'') + \frac{(A'A''+B'B''+C'C'')^2}{nn}$ (16)

Setzt man also $A(B'C''-C'B'')+B(C'A''-A'C'')+C(A'B''-B'A'')=\Delta$
so wird
$mm\left(\frac{\partial\partial\log m}{\partial t^2}+\frac{\partial\partial\log m}{\partial u^2}\right) = -\frac{(A'A'+B'B'+C'C'+\Delta)(A''A''+B''B''+C''C''[-+\Delta-]) - (A'A''+B'B''+C'C'')^2}{nn}$
$\frac{\partial\partial\log m}{\partial t^2}+\frac{\partial\partial\log m}{\partial u^2} = -\Delta$
Wir bemerken noch dass Auch haben wir uns überzeugt, dass in den Bedingungsgleichungen $\frac{\partial a'}{\partial u}=\frac{\partial\alpha'}{\partial t}$ &c. nichts weiter liegt, als dieses Resultat.
$B'C''-C'B''=A\Delta$
$C'A''-A'C''=B\Delta$ $\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)$[?]
$A'B''-B'A''=C\Delta$

Die Differentiation von $na$ und $n\alpha$ giebt
$na''+an''=\frac{\partial\partial A}{\partial t.\partial [-t-]u}+C\frac{\partial\partial B}{\partial u^2}-B\frac{\partial\partial C}{\partial u^2} = A^3+CB^4-BC^4$
$n\alpha''+\alpha n' = \frac{\partial\partial A}{\partial t.\partial u}+B\frac{\partial\partial C}{\partial t^2}-C\frac{\partial\partial B}{\partial t^2} = A^3+BC^2-CB^2$

$an''-\alpha n' = C(B^2+B^4)-B(C^2+C^4)$
Hieraus
[-mmn-] $mmn''=\alpha(A^2+A^4)+\beta(B^2+B^4)+\gamma(C^2+C^4)$
$mmn'=a(A^2+A^4)+b(B^2+B^4)+c(C^2+C^4)$
Nun ist ferner
$mmn'+mnm'=aA^2+bB^2+cC^2+\alpha A^3+\beta B^3+\gamma C^3$
$mmn''+mnm''=aA^3+bB^3+cC^3+\alpha A^4+\beta B^4+\gamma C^4$
also $mnm'=\alpha A^3+\beta B^3+\gamma C^3-aA^4-bB^4-cC^4$
$mnm''=-\alpha A^2-\beta B^2-\gamma C^2+aA^3+bB^3+cC^3$
Noch verdient bemerkt zu werden
$na'+an'=A^2-A\Delta+CB^3-BC^3$
$n\alpha''+\alpha n''=A^4-A\Delta+BC^3-CB^3$
also
$n'a+n''\alpha+n(\alpha''+a') = A^2+A^4-2A\Delta$
oder
$A^2+A^4=n'a+n''\alpha+(2\Delta-mmnn)A$
$B^2+B^4=n'b+n''\beta+(2\Delta-mmnn)B$
$C^2+C^4=n'c+n''\gamma+(2\Delta-mmnn)C$
[-$AA'+A''A''+AA^2+A$-]

$A^2=na'+an'+A\Delta$
$+Cnb''+\frac12C(bn''+\beta n')$
$+Bnc''+\frac12B(cn''+\gamma n')$
$A^3=na''+\frac12(an''+\alpha n')$
$A^4=n\alpha''+\alpha n''+A\Delta$
